A prior for the gap from validated detections

Source: R/fp_gap_prior.R
fp_gap_prior.Rd

Turns the precision of the classifier, measured on reviewed detections, into a prior for the gap \(\Delta\) between the true-detection and false-positive intercepts, and returns it in fp_priors().

Usage

fp_gap_prior(n_true, n_false, p11, psi, ndraws = 4000, ...)

Arguments

n_true, n_false

Numbers of reviewed detections confirmed as true and as false. They must be a random sample of the detections at the threshold of the analysis; detections picked for their high confidence overstate the precision.

p11

Probability that an occasion at an occupied site is a detection, at the reference values of the covariates. A single value, or a vector of draws that expresses its uncertainty.

psi

Occupancy probability at the reference values of the covariates. A single value, or a vector of draws.

ndraws

Number of draws used to propagate the uncertainty.

...

Further arguments for fp_priors().

Value

An fp_priors object; the derived values are in the attribute "gap_draws".

Details

In the model, an occasion at an occupied site is a detection with probability \(p_{11}\), which includes false alarms; an occasion at an unoccupied site, with probability \(p_{10}\). Assuming that false alarms occur at the same rate \(p_{10}\) at occupied sites, independently of true detections, the probability that an occasion holds a true detection is \(s = (p_{11} - p_{10}) / (1 - p_{10})\), and the share of automated detections that are true is $$\pi = \frac{\psi s}{\psi p_{11} + (1 - \psi) p_{10}}.$$ For given \(\pi\), \(p_{11}\) and \(\psi\), this has a single solution \(p_{10}\) between 0 and \(p_{11}\), the smaller root of a quadratic. The function draws \(\pi\) from its Beta(1 + n_true, 1 + n_false) posterior, solves for \(p_{10}\), computes \(\Delta = \mathrm{logit}(p_{11}) - \mathrm{logit}(p_{10})\), and uses the mean and standard deviation of the result as the parameters of the Normal prior on \(\Delta\). The model truncates that prior at zero; when most of the derived values are far from zero, as is usual, the truncation changes little. Guesses of p11 and psi usually come from a pilot fit or from earlier studies; give them as vectors when they are uncertain, so that the prior widens accordingly.

See also

fp_priors(), fp_read_validation()

Examples

# 46 of 50 randomly drawn detections were true; p11 and psi from a pilot
fp_gap_prior(n_true = 46, n_false = 4, p11 = 0.3, psi = 0.4)
#> <fp_priors> (logit scale)
#>   intercepts      ~ Normal(0, 1.5)
#>   slopes          ~ Normal(0, 2.5)
#>   fp_gap          ~ Normal(3.50353, 0.478711), truncated at 0
#>   sd_recorder     ~ half-Normal(0, 2)
#>   sd_fp_site      ~ half-Normal(0, 1)
# with uncertainty in p11
fp_gap_prior(46, 4, p11 = rbeta(1000, 30, 70), psi = 0.4)
#> <fp_priors> (logit scale)
#>   intercepts      ~ Normal(0, 1.5)
#>   slopes          ~ Normal(0, 2.5)
#>   fp_gap          ~ Normal(3.50994, 0.488533), truncated at 0
#>   sd_recorder     ~ half-Normal(0, 2)
#>   sd_fp_site      ~ half-Normal(0, 1)
